name: createElement()
description: Creates a new, detached element node of the given tag name that can be configured and inserted into the DOM.
parameters: tagName — the HTML tag name to create, e.g. 'div'.
returns: The newly created Element, not yet attached to the document.

name: appendChild()
description: Adds a node as the last child of a parent element.
notes: If the node already exists elsewhere in the DOM, it is moved rather than duplicated. Only accepts a single Node — use append() for multiple nodes or strings.

name: append() / prepend()
description: Insert one or more nodes or plain text strings at the end (append) or beginning (prepend) of a parent's children.
parameters: nodesOrStrings — any number of Node objects and/or strings.
notes: More flexible than appendChild()/insertBefore() since it accepts multiple arguments and raw text, but it does not return the inserted node.

name: removeChild() / remove()
description: Removes a node from the DOM. removeChild() is called on the parent with the child to remove; remove() is called directly on the element itself.
parameters: child — the child Node to remove (removeChild() only).
returns: removeChild() returns the removed node; remove() returns undefined.
example: item.remove(); // modern, no parent reference needed
notes: remove() is the simpler modern API and doesn't require a reference to the parent node.

name: replaceChild()
description: Replaces an existing child node of a parent with a new node.
parameters: newNode — the node to insert. oldNode — the existing child being replaced.
notes: element.replaceWith(newNode) is a more modern alternative called directly on the node to replace.

name: innerHTML
description: Gets or sets the HTML markup contained within an element, parsing any assigned string as HTML.
returns: A string of the element's inner HTML markup.
notes: Assigning user-supplied content via innerHTML can introduce XSS vulnerabilities — sanitize input or use textContent instead.

name: textContent vs innerText
description: textContent returns/sets all text within an element including hidden elements and without triggering layout, while innerText is layout-aware — it respects CSS styling (e.g. excludes display:none text) and triggers a reflow to compute.
example: el.textContent = 'safe'; // inserted as literal text, not parsed as HTML
notes: Prefer textContent for performance and for safely inserting plain text without HTML injection risk.

name: insertBefore()
description: Inserts a new node into a parent's children immediately before a specified reference node.
parameters: newNode — node to insert. referenceNode — existing child to insert before; null appends at the end.
notes: element.before(newNode) is a simpler modern alternative that doesn't require the parent.

name: insertAdjacentHTML()
description: Parses an HTML string and inserts the resulting nodes at a specified position relative to the element, without touching existing content.
parameters: position — one of 'beforebegin', 'afterbegin', 'beforeend', 'afterend'. text — the HTML string to parse and insert.
notes: More efficient than reassigning innerHTML since it avoids re-parsing and re-rendering existing content.

name: cloneNode()
description: Creates a copy of a node, optionally including all of its descendants.
parameters: deep — boolean; true clones the element and its entire subtree, false clones only the element itself.
returns: The cloned Node, detached from the document.
notes: Event listeners attached via addEventListener() are not copied to the clone.

name: setAttribute() for content
description: Changing certain attributes such as value, src or href via setAttribute() updates what the element displays or loads, effectively manipulating its rendered content.
parameters: name — attribute name. value — attribute value, coerced to a string.
notes: For form controls, prefer setting the .value property directly since setAttribute('value', ...) only changes the default value, not the live one.

name: DocumentFragment
description: Creates a lightweight, memory-only container for building a group of nodes off-DOM before inserting them all at once, avoiding multiple reflows.
notes: Appending a fragment to the DOM moves its children into place and leaves the fragment itself empty — useful for batch-inserting many elements efficiently.
